skill.name: whiteboard-animation
skill.description: Create whiteboard animations from SVG strokes and handwriting. Keep a marker tip aligned with each stroke, time reveals to narration, and prepare scenes for browser playback or video export.
skill.summary: Turn SVG line art into whiteboard animations with a marker hand that follows each stroke.
skill.author: iart-ai

security_audit.summary: The static alerts match Markdown or JavaScript syntax, SVG authoring instructions, and an abbreviated preview URL. Separate concerns are unpinned CLI invocations and screenshot helpers advertised as packaged but absent from the reviewed files. No evidence of prompt injection or intentional data exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: Screenshot and render instructions invoke unpinned CLI packages.
remediation.suggestion: Use project-local Playwright and Remotion versions pinned in a lockfile. Require the tools to be installed before verification, and do not fetch dependencies as part of the screenshot step.

remediation.issue: The documented screenshot helpers are not included in the reviewed skill.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the helper commands or ship reviewed copies and resolve them from the installed skill directory. Do not substitute scripts from the active project.

content.user_title: Create Whiteboard Animations from SVG Strokes
content.value_statement: A static illustration shows the finished diagram, but not how it takes shape. Reveal SVG strokes and handwriting in sequence, with a marker hand and timing that follows your narration.
actual_capabilities: Reveal open SVG strokes in drawing order and move a marker tip along the visible end of each stroke.
Animate handwriting as ordered glyph strokes or reveal live text with a moving mask.
Reveal fills after outlines and clear the board with a wipe or reverse drawing.
Time drawings and pauses to narration and use Remotion for frame-based video rendering.
Build a standalone HTML scene with timestamp previews and a static reduced-motion state.
limitations: Raster sketches and filled artwork need open stroke paths or separate outlines for a true stroke reveal.
The reviewed package does not include a marker hand asset or the documented screenshot helper scripts.
Detailed handwriting requires stroke paths for each glyph. A text mask reveals the word without tracing each letter.
Narrated video export requires a separate Remotion project and a voiceover track. The standalone HTML example does not produce a video file.

use_cases.title: Explain a Concept Step by Step
use_cases.description: Draw each part of a classroom diagram in the order it is introduced, then pause on the completed illustration.

use_cases.title: Animate a Logo Reveal
use_cases.description: Reveal an SVG logo outline with a marker hand, then bring in the fill and hold on the completed logo.

use_cases.title: Produce a Narrated Training Clip
use_cases.description: Match each drawing to a voiceover line and clear the board between sections before rendering the video in Remotion.

prompt_templates.title: Animate One Stroke
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a standalone HTML page that draws my SVG arrow over two seconds and holds on the completed shape. Include a static reduced-motion state.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Preview a simple SVG line drawing in a browser.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Marker Hand
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate my three SVG paths in order using the supplied marker hand image. Keep the marker tip on the visible stroke and lift the hand between paths.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Animate a drawing with several strokes.

prompt_templates.title: Match Drawings to Narration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my narration transcript to plan three drawings, one per spoken line. Add a handwritten label to each drawing and wipe the board between sections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Plan the visual sequence before rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Frame-Based Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Port my SVG storyboard into my existing Remotion project and use the voiceover timestamps to place each drawing. Provide start, mid-stroke, and end frames for review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Review a narrated composition before video export.

output_examples.input: Animate an SVG lightbulb, then reveal a yellow fill.
output: A browser scene draws the outline before revealing the yellow fill.
A midpoint preview shows the marker tip aligned with the visible end of the stroke.
The reduced-motion version shows the completed bulb without the marker hand.

output_examples.input: Plan a two-part animation for a voiceover about collecting and sorting feedback.
output: The first drawing shows a suggestion box while the narrator describes collecting feedback.
After a short pause, the board wipes left to right.
The next drawing uses arrows to sort feedback into labeled groups as the narrator names them.

best_practices: Use open paths in drawing order, and add separate fills after their outlines finish.
Calibrate the marker tip against a test path and inspect a frame in the middle of a stroke.
Match drawing time to the spoken line and include a short pause before the next illustration.
anti_patterns: Animate a filled compound shape as if it were a single pen stroke.
Move one marker hand across active strokes that are drawing at the same time.
Review only the finished frame, where marker drift and incorrect draw order may be hard to detect.

faq.question: Can I open a scene directly in a browser?
faq.answer: Yes. A standalone HTML scene can contain the SVG, marker artwork, and animation script without a build step.

faq.question: Can I use a PNG sketch?
faq.answer: Yes, as source artwork. Redraw or trace it into open SVG strokes before animating the lines.

faq.question: Can it animate handwritten labels?
faq.answer: Yes. Use ordered glyph strokes for realistic handwriting, or reveal live text with a moving mask.

faq.question: Can I export an MP4 with narration?
faq.answer: Yes, through a separate Remotion project. Supply the voiceover track and time the animation to its spoken lines.

faq.question: How can I check the marker alignment?
faq.answer: Pause the preview in the middle of a stroke. The marker tip should sit at the visible end of that stroke.

faq.question: What happens when reduced motion is enabled?
faq.answer: The scene shows the completed board without drawing animation or the marker hand.
